Content:
Let's prove the following proposition.

Content:
[MATH: \underbrace{mn \text{ is even}}_{P(m,n)}
\quad\Rightarrow\quad
\underbrace{m \text{ is even or } n \text{ is even}}_{Q(m,n)}]

Content:
To prove [MATH: P \Rightarrow Q,] it suffices to prove the contrapositive [MATH: \neg Q \Rightarrow \neg P.]

Content:
[MATH: \neg\left(m \text{ is even or } n \text{ is even}\right)
\quad\Rightarrow\quad
\neg\left(mn \text{ is even}\right)]

Content:
Negating the right-hand-side of our implication is straightforward:

Content:
[MATH: \neg\left(m \text{ is even or } n \text{ is even}\right)
\quad\Rightarrow\quad
mn \text{ is odd}]

Content:
To negate the statement "[MATH: m] is even or [MATH: n] is even," we use De Morgan's law for disjunctions.

Content:
[MATH: ¬(mis even ornis even)|⇔¬(mis even∨nis even); ⇔¬(mis even)∧¬(nis even); ⇔mis odd∧nis odd; ⇔mis odd andnis odd]

Content:
So, let's write down the contrapositive of our original statement.

Content:
> The contrapositive form of the given statement is as follows:
> [MATH: m \text{ is odd and } n \text{ is odd}
> \quad\Rightarrow\quad
> mn \text{ is odd}]

Content:
We start by using the fact that [MATH: m] and [MATH: n] are odd.

Content:
> If [MATH: m] and [MATH: n] are odd, then
> [MATH: m = 2a+1
> \quad\text{and}\quad
> n = 2b+1,]
> where [MATH: a] and [MATH: b] are integers.

Content:
We substitute [MATH: m=2a+1] and [MATH: n=2b+1] into the expression [MATH: mn] and show it is odd by writing it as one larger than a multiple of [MATH: 2.]

Content:
> Therefore,
> [MATH: mn|= (2a + 1)(2b + 1); = 4ab + 2a + 2b + 1; = 2(2ab + a + b)_(⏟)_(c) + 1.]

Content:
Now, if we define another integer [MATH: c=2ab+a+b] (highlighted above), we have that [MATH: mn = 2c+1,] which shows that [MATH: mn] is indeed one larger than a multiple of [MATH: 2.]

Content:
> Let [MATH: c=2ab+a+b.] Since [MATH: a] and [MATH: b] are integers, we have that [MATH: c] is an integer.
>
> Hence, we have
> [MATH: mn|= 2(2ab + a + b)_(⏟)_(c) + 1; = 2c + 1,]
> which is one larger than a multiple of [MATH: 2.]

Content:
Finally, we write our conclusion.

Content:
> Therefore, [MATH: mn] is odd.
